subject: Dedicated capacity decisions, trade-offs and pilot plan (Synthetix Labs)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha@synthetix.com>, Diego Ramirez <diego@synthetix.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity decisions, trade-offs and pilot plan (Synthetix Labs)

Hi Aisha, Diego,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — solid discussion and good alignment on the core goals. Below is a concise recap plus the pilot / decision path I recommend to validate isolation, scaling, and SLA behavior before a larger reserved commitment.

1) Problem / pain points we heard
- Latency variability impacting interactive search features (spikes during business hours).
- Need for predictable unit economics for heavy vector + chat workloads.
- Regulatory requirement to keep production traffic within US-only regions.

2) Goals you stated
- Baseline production throughput: ~600 requests / minute (steady).
- Peak windows up to ~2,500 requests / minute for short bursts.
- P95 generation latency target: ~<450 ms for 512-token typical responses.
- Operational: SOC2 + audit logs, dedicated pool for data isolation.

3) Recommended starting configuration (Redwood proposal)
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4–8 GPU equivalent to start (we recommend starting at 4 reserved for pilot, option to convert to 8 after validation).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool (isolated compute, customer-only queues).
- Burst: allow automatic burst to a shared pool up to 16 GPUs for peak windows; option to extend burst to 32 with procurement approval.
- Inference optimizations: INT8 quantization path + KV/prefix caching to reduce per-token cost and lower long-tail latency.

4) SLA and performance expectations
- Pilot SLA (validation phase): target 99.9% monthly uptime, benchmark p95 < 550 ms for pilot traffic profile.
- Long-term SLA: standard reserved offering targets 99.95% and a contractual p95 target we can finalize in the MSA.

5) Cost/ops trade-offs (high level)
- Reserved GPUs reduce unit cost; smaller reserved pool + burst gives cost flexibility during unknown peak patterns.
- More reserved capacity lowers burst dependency but increases committed spend.

6) Attachments included
- Synthetix_MAPlan_v1.pdf (mutual action plan draft)
- initial_sla_draft.docx (SLA sketch for procurement)
- capacity_cost_model.csv (ballpark pricing by reserved size and burst behavior)

7) Proposed next steps and owners
- Aisha: confirm pilot scope (4 reserved + burst to 16) or propose alternate sizing by 2027-06-07.
- Diego / Procurement: share purchasing cadence and preferred PO terms by 2027-06-18.
- Redwood (Mina/Rishi): provide a formal pilot proposal, pricing options for 4/8/16 reserved by 2027-06-03 (see attached).
- Schedule: pilot kickoff call week of 2027-06-21 once PO/DocuSign is in place.

If that summary matches your notes, we can wire up the DocuSign and lock dates. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk the MA plan line-by-line.

Thanks,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity decisions, trade-offs and pilot plan (Synthetix Labs)

Thanks Mina — this is a helpful and thorough recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we circulate to procurement: 

- Sizing: I like the pilot-first approach. Can you include 3 discrete price points for comparison (4 reserved, 8 reserved, 16 reserved) in the proposal? Diego will need those for our internal TCO analysis.
- Burst behavior: during peak events we expect some minutes-long spikes that could push well past 2,500 rpm. How does Redwood bill for burst usage vs reserved? Is there a hard cap on burst if the shared pool saturates?
- Compliance: confirm SOC2 Type II readiness and whether the isolated pool meets our data residency ask (US-only).

I've cc'd our procurement lead (diego@synthetix.com) — Diego, can you confirm your preferred contract route (PO vs SOW) and the person who will do payment terms?

Also attaching our procurement intake form (procurement_contact.xlsx) so you can see the fields Diego will require.

Best,
Aisha

Thanks Aisha — quick answers and a sizing note from infra: 

1) Pricing snapshot (monthly, list; final pricing in proposal)
- 4 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent): $28,000 / month (includes isolated pool + 500GB KV cache retention).
- 8 reserved GPUs: $52,000 / month.
- 16 reserved GPUs: $98,000 / month.
- Burst: billed at usage rate based on consumed vGPU-minutes above reserved. For pilot we can cap burst spend to a negotiated monthly threshold to avoid surprising invoices.

2) Burst capacity details
- Burst uses available shared pool managed by Redwood. If shared pool saturates, requests are queued with prioritized routing rules (customer can choose graceful degradation, fallback to smaller model variants, or fail-fast).
- We recommend a burst-to-16 plan with a monetary cap for pilot (we propose $6k cap for the first 30 days).

3) Compliance / residency
- Redwood Private + Dedicated offerings run in US regions and support SOC2 Type II controls; the isolated pool option meets your data residency and audit-log requirements. We will include SOC2 attestation in the procurement pack.

4) Sizing rationale
- Starting at 4 reserved GPUs reduces committed spend while letting us validate traffic patterns. The ability to burst to 16 provides headroom for the short event spikes you described. If the pilot shows sustained peak utilization, converting to 8 reserved typically provides a good cost/liveness trade-off.

Action: I'll add these numbers to the formal proposal and include an explicit burst cap line item.

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations. Moving to concrete next steps so we can lock timelines: 

Agreed pilot scope (as discussed):
- 30-day pilot: 4 reserved GPUs (isolated pool), automatic burst up to 16 GPUs, burst spend cap $6,000 for pilot window.
- Pilot SLA: 99.9% target for pilot; we will run benchmark profile and provide p95 measurements (target < 550 ms for your 512-token use cases).
- Success metrics:
  - Average p95 latency under pilot load
  - Cost per 1M tokens (post quantization + caching)
  - Error rate < 1% and no data residency violations

Owners and immediate asks:
- Aisha: confirm acceptance of pilot scope and the $6k burst cap by 2027-06-07 so we can issue the DocuSign.
- Diego: confirm procurement route (PO vs SOW) and share procurement contact email by 2027-06-10.
- Rishi: finalize the formal proposal and attach the pricing lines mentioned above by EOD 2027-06-03 (attached: capacity_cost_model.csv).

I will spin up a DocuSign with the pilot MSA + burst cap and send today if we get a green light. If you prefer a short sync to walk the MA plan, I'm free 2027-06-04 morning PST.

Look forward to partnering on the pilot — we’ll make it low friction and instrumented so you can make a clean convert/no-convert decision after 30 days.

Thanks,
Mina
